title: Great News for Taiwan Semiconductor Stock Investors | TSM Earnings Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkev Tatavosianc reviews Taiwan Semiconductor's Q3 2026 earnings: revenue $47B, up 41% year on year, with gross margins over 66% and operating margins approaching the high-50s, both above the high end of guidance. Leading-edge nodes are ramping fast — 2nm rose from 3% to 8% of wafer revenue in one quarter and 3nm is 33% — while high-performance computing (AI) reached 68% of revenue as smartphone share fell to 21% because handset makers order less as component prices rise. TSMC reiterated 2026 capex of $60–64B against sold-out capacity and customer deposits booked through 2027 into 2028, but again guided long-term gross margins down as new technology and overseas fabs ramp. The stock fell 1.8% on the print despite being up over 40% in 2026; at $422, 18.8x forward earnings, Parkev reiterates his BUY with high conviction against a $584 DCF fair value, flagging China/Taiwan geopolitics and a possible AI slowdown as the main risks.

calls.video_title: Great News for Taiwan Semiconductor Stock Investors | TSM Earnings Analysis
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY with high conviction after Q3 earnings: revenue $47B (+41% YoY), gross margins over 66%, forward P/E 18.8 — relatively cheap for this growth, margins and moat; meaningful upside to his $584 DCF.
calls.base_case: 2nm ramped 3%→8% of wafer revenue and 3nm is 33%; HPC is 68% of revenue; capex guided $60–64B in 2026 against sold-out capacity and customer deposits/pre-orders booked through 2027 into 2028.
calls.bull_case: Premium pricing and elevated utilization keep offsetting the guided margin drag from new technology and overseas fabs for longer than management expects.
calls.bear_case: Geopolitics (China/Taiwan) is the biggest risk; long-term gross margins guided down as manufacturing diversifies, and AI demand could slow in a few years.
